headline: Evaluation design reshapes performance claims for biological foundation and ML models
label: Benchmarking Biological Machine Learning Models
summary: Recent preprints scrutinize negative sampling, label noise, and baseline choice in biological prediction benchmarks.
synthesis: The dominant thread is scrutiny of how biological prediction models are evaluated. Several items show that evaluation choices, not model architecture alone, determine reported performance: constructed negatives alter PPI model rankings and AUPRC, and degree-associated negative-set topology and novelty leakage drive apparent discrimination on the Guo yeast benchmark. NoiTox flags possible label noise in peptide toxicity datasets. For foundation models, single-cell evaluations find advantage confined to low-data regimes across 868 disease and 65 cell-type tasks, while layer-wise probing shows intermediate layers can outperform final-layer embeddings. DNA foundation model embeddings yield only modest gains over k-mer composition across 57 datasets. Remaining items apply model classes to affinity prediction, CRISPR off-target and base-editing outcomes, RNA localization, and reverse target fishing. The new element is systematic, quantitative auditing of benchmark construction rather than architecture alone.
